subject: Logic
title: The Teleporter Paradox
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Teleporter Paradox.

hook.text: A teleporter scans you, destroys the original, and builds a perfect copy at the destination. Did you travel—or die?

buildup.text: The copy has all your memories, personality, and feelings. Everyone else sees no difference.

discovery.text: But the original was destroyed. If continuity of consciousness matters, the copy is someone new who thinks they're you.

twist.text: What if the machine malfunctions and doesn't destroy the original? Now there are two of you. Which is real?

climax.text: The paradox forces a choice: is identity about material continuity, psychological continuity, or something else?

punchline.text: Same atoms, same memories. Same person?

quiz.question: What does the teleporter paradox question?
options: Whether personal identity requires physical continuity
